title: Famine
lead: Famine runs through the Bible, from Abram's journey to Egypt to the black horse of Revelation. It drives families from their land (Genesis 12:10; Ruth 1:1), tests faith, comes as a warning that calls people back to God (Amos 4:6–8; Haggai 1:10–11), and in its worst form, under siege, brings parents to eat their children (Leviticus 26:29; 2 Kings 6:28–29; Lamentations 4:10). God is the one who sends rain and food, and the one who rescues from famine (Genesis 41; Psalm 104:27–28; Acts 14:17).

sections.b: Famine moves the story of Genesis: Abram goes down to Egypt (Genesis 12:10), Isaac stays in Gerar and is blessed (Genesis 26:1, 12), and Joseph stores grain for seven years of hunger (Genesis 41:35–36), so that God "planned it for good ... to keep many people alive" (Genesis 50:20). Elimelech's family leaves Bethlehem for Moab (Ruth 1:1). David seeks the LORD in three years of famine (2 Samuel 21:1), and Elijah announces years with "no dew and no rain" (1 Kings 17:1).
sections.refs: Genesis 12:10; Genesis 26:1–12; Genesis 41:35–36; Genesis 50:20; Ruth 1:1; 2 Samuel 21:1; 1 Kings 17:1

sections.b: The covenant warnings of Leviticus 26 and Deuteronomy 28 include a sky "like iron" (Leviticus 26:19) and, at the last, the siege in which parents eat their children (Leviticus 26:29; Deuteronomy 28:53–57). The prophets record both: Amos lists hunger, drought and blight, each ending "yet you did not turn back to me" (Amos 4:6–9), and Lamentations mourns Jerusalem's children (Lamentations 2:20; 4:10). The aim of the warnings is return, not ruin.
sections.refs: Leviticus 26:19–29; Deuteronomy 28:23–24; Deuteronomy 28:53–57; Amos 4:6–9; 2 Kings 6:25–29; Lamentations 2:20; Lamentations 4:10

sections.b: Against famine the Bible sets the God who opens his hand to feed every living thing (Psalm 145:15–16), who fed Israel with manna, and whose Son fed crowds with bread and fish (John 6:11–13). Revelation's rider with the scale (Revelation 6:5–6) belongs to the troubles before the end, which give way to a people who "will never go hungry again" (Revelation 7:16).
sections.refs: Psalm 104:27–28; Psalm 145:15–16; Exodus 16:4; John 6:11–13; Revelation 6:5–6; Revelation 7:16
